paper_metadata.title: Study of NiAl-based alloy parts produced by metal injection moulding

evidence.quote: NiAl–(Cr, Mo, Zr) alloys were successfully prepared by metal injection moulding (MIM) technique as well as avoiding common defects produced by other processing techniques.

other.feedstock: 62 vol.-% alloy powder, 38 vol.-% paraffin-based binder

evidence.quote: All samples were moulded using a TIANJIAN PL860/290 machine at 100 MPa and the injection nozzle temperature was 160°C.
First, solvent debinding in trichloroethylene at 40°C for 10 h was applied (GUO HUA HH-8, China).
Then, thermal debinding and pre-sintering process were conducted at ∼ 600°C and 900°C for 2 h under ﬂowing H 2 gas in the tube furnace (GSL-1400x, China).

The ﬁnal sintering process was performed in a vacuum sintering furnace (ZRC85-25T, China) under a vacuum of 10 −3 mbar between 1360°C and 1400°C with four sintering time of 1, 2, 3 and 4 h, followed by furnace cooling.

phases_and_microstructures.name: crack deflection by Cr(Mo) phase toughening

evidence.quote: the cracks were mainly formed in the NiAl matrix phase and terminated at the edge of the Cr(Mo) phase, as shown in Figure 10 (a). The cracks can be resisted by the toughening e ﬀects of Cr(Mo) phase and improve the fracture strain of the alloy.
The yield strength of NiAl-based alloy is signi ﬁcantly increased because of the high strength Cr(Mo) phase.

When the sintering temperature is in the range of 1360– 1390°C, the increase of sintering temperature is conducive to the di ﬀusion of metal powder, but the further increase of temperature will lead to sample distortion.
